title: K-flat comparison of the actual support sequences
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$, $j:U\hookrightarrow P$ be a closed-open pair of schemes and let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Work on ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $T_W=-\otimes_A^LB_W$ and let $\operatorname{Res}$ be exact restriction of scalars [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Suppose $L\in D(P_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $TL$ and $Rj_*j^*TL$ are bounded below, and so are $L$, $Rj_*j^*L$ and $T_PRj_{*,A}j^*L$. Choose a degreewise-injective K-injective representative $I$ of $L$, a K-flat flat-term resolution $Q\to B_P$, and a functorial degreewise-injective K-injective replacement $a:N=\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes_A I)\to J$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution, lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence]. Let $H_A$ and the actual short exact support sequences be those of [lem-pur-etale-injective-support-sequence]. Tensoring the support sequence of $I$ with $Q$ gives a degreewise short exact sequence. There is a natural map from this sequence to the support sequence of $J$ whose middle map is $a$ and whose last map is
$$Q\otimes_A j_*j^*I\to j_*(j^*Q\otimes_A j^*I)\xrightarrow{j_*j^*a}j_*j^*J.$$
Its first map is the induced map of kernels. The resulting morphism of distinguished triangles has middle map the identity of $\operatorname{Res}(TL)$ and right map the restriction of the canonical coefficient projection $T_PRj_{*,A}j^*L\to Rj_{*,B}j^*TL$. In particular, if that right map is invertible, its first map is invertible. These claims include compatibility with the connecting arrow and do not impose a strict $B$-module structure on $Q$.

proof.text: All complexes in the diagram are $A_P$-module complexes. In particular $a:N\to J$ is the functorial replacement in that category, not a replacement in $B_P$-modules. Put $S=i_*H_A(I)$, $C=j_*j^*I$, $S'=i_*H_A(J)$, and $C'=j_*j^*J$. The support-sequence lemma gives actual short exact rows $0\to S\xrightarrow{s}I\xrightarrow{r_I}C\to0$ and $0\to S'\xrightarrow{s'}J\xrightarrow{r_J}C'\to0$, with $S'=\ker r_J$. The fixed-K-flat tensor lemma identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes I)$ with $L\otimes_A^LB_P$, and likewise identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes C)$ with $(Rj_{*,A}j^*L)\otimes_A^LB_P$; use the signed interchange of tensor factors when placing $B_P$ on the right. The canonical scalar/tensor identification in the scalar-mate lemma identifies the first object with $\operatorname{Res}(T_PL)$. Identify $Q_{!D}J$ with this same object by the inverse of $Q_{!D}a$, where $Q_{!D}$ denotes localization. Thus the localized middle map is the identity under the specified identifications.

source.place: Tags 06YS/06YU (K-flat resolutions and derived tensor), 093X (injective support row); the blueprint locality argument, interpreted in ordinary A-module complexes

proof.text: For each pair $(p,q)$, tensor the degree-$q$ exact row with the flat sheaf $Q^p$. Flatness means that this tensor functor is exact, so $0\to Q^p\otimes S^q\to Q^p\otimes I^q\to Q^p\otimes C^q\to0$ is exact. In total degree $n$ take the sum over $p+q=n$. This sum is the filtered colimit of the finite subsums: the index consists of finite subsets of the integer-indexed set of pairs, ordered by inclusion. Each finite subsum is exact because kernels and cokernels of finite biproduct maps are computed componentwise; exactness of filtered colimits therefore proves exactness of the whole row. With the total differential $d_Q\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d$, the inclusions and quotients commute with both differential terms. Consequently $0\to\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes S)\to N\to\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes C)\to0$ is a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes. This uses flat terms as well as K-flatness; no convergence of a double-complex spectral sequence is used.

source.place: Tag 03ER (sites-modules-definition-flat), item (3); Tag 03DB (sites-modules-lemma-limits-colimits); total differential of Tag 012Z

proof.text: Let $c_j:j^*\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes C)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}(j^*Q\otimes j^*C)$ be the cochain pullback/tensor comparison. Form the chain map $h=(j^*a)\,(1\otimes\varepsilon^0_{j^*I})\,c_j:j^*\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes C)\to j^*J$, where $\varepsilon^0:j^*j_*\to1$ is the ordinary counit. Define $v=j_*h\,\eta_{\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes C)}$. By termwise adjunction this is a chain map to $C'$. Equivalently $v$ is the displayed map in the statement: its first factor is adjoint to $(1\otimes\varepsilon^0_{j^*I})c_j$, and its second factor is $j_*j^*a$. On a bidegree summand $x\otimes y$, the first factor restricts $x$ to $U$ and evaluates the restricted $j_*j^*I$ section by its counit. No assertion that $j_*$ commutes with infinite sums is needed: the map out of the total direct sum is induced by these summand maps. The cochain comparison and the degree-zero units and counits preserve bidegrees, so both differential terms, including $(-1)^p$, commute with this map.

source.place: Tags 03EL/07A4 (cochain tensor/pullback comparison); termwise inverse-image adjunction and its unit/counit

proof.text: The right square commutes already as a square of complexes: $v(1\otimes r_I)=r_Ja$. Indeed, take ordinary $j^*\dashv j_*$ transposes. By naturality of $c_j$, the transpose of the left side is $j^*a$ composed with $1\otimes(\varepsilon^0_{j^*I}j^*r_I)$, after the cochain tensor comparison. The parentheses equal the identity by the adjunction triangle identity, since $r_I=\eta_I$. The transpose of the right side is $\varepsilon^0_{j^*J}j^*\eta_Jj^*a=j^*a$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves the equality. Thus $a$ sends the kernel of the top quotient into $\ker r_J=S'$. By the kernel universal property there is a unique $u:\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes S)\to S'$ with $s'u=a(1\otimes s)$. This is a chain map: after the monomorphism $s'$ its differential equation is the chain-map equation for $a(1\otimes s)$. These constructions are natural in chain maps of $I$: naturality gives the middle and right squares, and cancellation of $s'$ gives the first.

source.place: The adjunction identities; kernels in the actual support rows of Tag 093X

proof.text: Apply the short-exact-complex triangle lemma to the two rows and their strict morphism $(u,a,v)$. It supplies distinguished triangles and, crucially, the equation $(Q_{!D}u)[1]\,\delta_{\mathrm{top}}=\delta_{\mathrm{bottom}}\,Q_{!D}v$ for their connecting maps. The bottom row is the actual support triangle of $J$ by the support-sequence lemma. The top row has the tensor-model objects identified in Step 1. Thus this is a morphism of the asserted distinguished triangles, with middle component the identity. This conclusion uses the functorial boundary attached to these exact rows; it does not choose an arbitrary third map completing two triangle squares.

We identify the localized right component, retaining its specified map. The support-sequence lemma gives the canonical computation $Q_{!D}C'=Rj_{*,A}j^*(Q_{!D}J)$. Under this computation $Q_{!D}v$ is the canonical derived comparison composed with the localized chain adjunct from Step 3. The chain-transpose lemma says its derived transpose is exactly $Q_{!D}h$. Also its counit equation identifies $Q_{!D}(\varepsilon^0_{j^*I})$ with the derived counit at $j^*L$ under $Q_{!D}C=Rj_{*,A}j^*L$. The pullback lemma makes $j^*Q$ flat-term K-flat, so both $c_j$ and $j^*a$ represent the canonical derived tensor/pullback comparison and the identity on $j^*\operatorname{Res}(T_PL)$. Consequently, after the signed interchange putting $B$ second, $Q_{!D}h$ is precisely $(\varepsilon_{j,j^*L}\otimes^L1_{B_U})\,c_{Rj_*j^*L,B_P}$. By the definition of the projection-formula map, the adjunction bijection now identifies $Q_{!D}v$ with $\mathrm{PF}_j(j^*L,B_P)$, with target $Rj_{*,A}(j^*L\otimes_A^LB_U)$. The identification of maps follows from equality of transposes, not merely from an isomorphism of their source and target objects.

source.place: Tags 0FPI/07A6 (derived adjunction counit square), 0G7E/07A4 (K-flat pullback and tensor models); projection map by its defining transpose

proof.text: Apply the scalar-mate projection lemma to $f=j$ and its input $j^*L$. Exact inverse image makes $j^*L$ and $j^*T_PL$ bounded below. The other required source bound is exactly the assumed bound on $T_PRj_{*,A}j^*L$. The canonical inverse-image/scalar comparison identifies $T_Uj^*L$ with $j^*T_PL$. The canonical direct-image/restriction isomorphism identifies $Rj_{*,A}\operatorname{Res}(j^*T_PL)$ with $\operatorname{Res}(Rj_{*,B}j^*T_PL)$. Under these identifications the scalar-mate lemma identifies the map of Step 6 with the restriction of the canonical coefficient projection $T_PRj_{*,A}j^*L\to Rj_{*,B}j^*T_PL$. The assumed bounds on $T_PL$ and its open direct image ensure that this is the stated bounded-below comparison. No restricted $B$-injective complex is used as an $A$-injective resolution: the support row was built from the $A$-injective replacement $J$.

source.place: Tag 0GL6 (more-etale-remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings), projection/scalar identification; Tags 0D6J/03FD for canonical coefficient-restriction comparison

proof.text: If the right component is invertible, the middle identity and the right component are two isomorphisms in the morphism of distinguished triangles constructed in Step 5. The triangle two-isomorphisms lemma gives invertibility of its first component. Functorial replacement makes all squares above natural on chain maps; the kernel uniqueness and the functorial boundary of Step 5 give the corresponding naturality of the complete triangle diagram, including its connecting square. Every chain map used in the construction is $A$-linear; the $B$-linear projection was invoked only after passing to the derived category and restricting scalars. Therefore no step equips $Q$ with a strict $B$-module structure.
